meta.title: Mark the Phrase Breaks: Usage Debates and Style Guides

questions.prompt: A style guide states that a comma should not be placed before the coordinating conjunction when it joins only two short independent clauses. Which sentence follows that rule?
choices: The sun set, and the lights came on.
The sun set and the lights came on.
The sun set; and the lights came on.
The sun set: and the lights came on.
questions.explanation: When two brief independent clauses are joined by a coordinating conjunction, the guide omits the comma, so 'The sun set and the lights came on.' is correct.

questions.prompt: A style guide requires commas around a conjunctive adverb that interrupts a sentence. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: The device works normally however, only after a restart.
The device works normally, however, only after a restart.
The device works, normally however, only after a restart.
The device works normally, however only, after a restart.
questions.explanation: The conjunctive adverb however is enclosed by commas because it interrupts the main sentence.
questions.skill: Setting off an interrupting conjunctive adverb

questions.prompt: A style guide sets off a vocative that interrupts a sentence with commas. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: Take your seats everyone before the curtain rises.
Take your seats, everyone before the curtain rises.
Take your seats, everyone, before the curtain rises.
Take your seats, everyone, before, the curtain rises.
questions.explanation: The interrupting vocative everyone is enclosed by commas on both sides.

questions.prompt: A style guide requires a colon after "as follows" when it introduces a list. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: The steps are as follows: gather data, analyze results, write report.
The steps are as follows; gather data, analyze results, write report.
The steps are as follows, gather data, analyze results, write report.
The steps are as follows gather data, analyze results, write report.
questions.explanation: The guide uses a colon after "as follows" to introduce the list.
questions.topic: Mark the Phrase Breaks - Usage Debates and Style Guides

questions.prompt: A style guide spells website as one word and forms its plural by adding s. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: The archive contains thousands of old website.
The archive contains thousands of old web sites.
The archive contains thousands of old websites.
The archive contains thousands of old website's.
questions.explanation: The plural form websites follows the style guide's one-word spelling and regular plural rule.
questions.skill: Applying a style guide to spelling and pluralization

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly follows the style-guide rule for a restrictive relative clause?
choices: The hikers, who carried maps, followed the marked trail.
The hikers who carried maps followed the marked trail.
The hikers who, carried maps followed the marked trail.
The hikers who carried maps, followed the marked trail.
questions.explanation: A restrictive relative clause identifies the hikers and is not set off by commas in the first sentence.

questions.prompt: A style guide prohibits a comma between a professional title and the name that follows it. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: Professor Chen explained the results.
Professor, Chen explained the results.
Professor Chen, explained the results.
Professor, Chen, explained the results.
questions.explanation: A professional title is not separated from the following name by a comma.
questions.topic: Usage Debates and Style Guides — Marking Phrase Breaks

questions.prompt: A style guide requires a hyphen in the compound modifier well-known when it appears before a noun. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: The article cited, a well-known example of adaptation.
The article cited a well known example of adaptation.
The article cited a well-known example of adaptation.
The article cited a well-known example, of adaptation.
questions.explanation: The hyphen joins the elements of the compound modifier well-known in the phrase well-known example.
questions.skill: Applying a hyphenation rule for compound modifiers

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly marks the phrase break before the coordinating conjunction joining two independent clauses?
choices: The novel was difficult, but the ending was satisfying.
The novel was difficult but, the ending was satisfying.
The novel was difficult but the ending, was satisfying.
The novel, was difficult but the ending was satisfying.
questions.explanation: The first sentence places a comma before the coordinating conjunction joining two independent clauses.
questions.skill: Marking phrase breaks before coordinating conjunctions

questions.prompt: A style guide follows legal citation style: v. is preceded by a space, and no comma appears around it. Which case name follows the rule?
choices: Brown v. Board, of Education
Brown, v. Board of Education
Brown v, Board of Education
Brown v. Board of Education
questions.explanation: The abbreviation v. correctly follows Brown with a space and is not separated by commas.

questions.prompt: A style guide sets off an appositive at the end of a sentence with a comma before it and a period after it. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: The winning design, was created by a first-year student, Elena Ortiz.
The winning design was created, by a first-year student, Elena Ortiz.
The winning design was created by, a first-year student, Elena Ortiz.
The winning design was created by a first-year student, Elena Ortiz.
questions.explanation: The appositive Elena Ortiz renames the noun phrase a first-year student and is set off at the end of the sentence.

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly marks the phrase break after the introductory dependent clause?
choices: Because the trail was flooded, the group took a longer route.
Because the trail was flooded the group, took a longer route.
Because the trail, was flooded the group took a longer route.
Because the trail was flooded the group took a longer, route.
questions.explanation: A comma separates the introductory dependent clause from the main clause in the first sentence.
questions.skill: Marking phrase breaks after introductory dependent clauses

questions.prompt: A style guide requires a colon to introduce a list of required materials. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: The required materials were paper, pens and ink.
The required materials were, paper, pens and ink.
The required materials were; paper, pens and ink.
The required materials were: paper, pens and ink.
questions.explanation: The colon signals that the words after it form a list of required materials.
questions.topic: Mark the Phrase Breaks - Usage Debates and Style Guides

questions.prompt: A style guide requires a comma before respectively when it links two results in the same order. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: The runners placed first and second respectively.
The runners placed first and second, respectively.
The runners placed, first and second, respectively.
The runners placed first, and second respectively.
questions.explanation: The comma before respectively marks its connection to the two results in the stated order.

questions.prompt: Which sentence follows the style guide that requires spaced em dashes around a parenthetical phrase?
choices: The results — unexpected and surprising — were published yesterday.
The results—unexpected and surprising—were published yesterday.
The results, unexpected and surprising, were published yesterday.
The results (unexpected and surprising) were published yesterday.
questions.explanation: The correct sentence follows the style guide that requires spaced em dashes around a parenthetical insertion.
questions.topic: Mark the Phrase Breaks - Usage Debates and Style Guides

questions.prompt: A sentence begins with the conjunctive adverb However. Where should the phrase break appear?
choices: However, the scoreboard showed the visitors had one point left.
However the scoreboard showed the visitors had one point left.
However; the scoreboard showed the visitors had one point left.
However: the scoreboard showed the visitors had one point left.
questions.explanation: A comma should follow the introductory conjunctive adverb However before the main clause begins.
questions.skill: Marking a break after an introductory conjunctive adverb

questions.prompt: A style guide requires commas around a nonrestrictive participial phrase that adds information. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: The finalists smiling at the crowd waved to their families.
The finalists, smiling at the crowd, waved to their families.
The finalists, smiling at the crowd waved to their families.
The finalists smiling at the crowd, waved to their families.
questions.explanation: The commas correctly set off the nonrestrictive participial phrase smiling at the crowd.
questions.topic: Usage Debates and Style Guides — Marking Phrase Breaks

questions.prompt: A style guide does not place a comma before a quotation that functions as a complete sentence. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: The poster read, 'The gate opens at eight.'
The poster read 'The gate opens at eight.'
The poster read 'The gate opens at eight,'
The poster read, 'The gate opens at eight'
questions.explanation: Because the quotation forms a complete sentence, the style guide does not require a comma before it.

questions.prompt: A style guide requires commas around a dependent clause inserted in the middle of a sentence. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: The report although it was delayed, was released on time.
The report, although it was delayed, was released on time.
The report, although it was delayed was released on time.
The report although it was delayed was released on time.
questions.explanation: The paired commas set off although it was delayed as an inserted dependent clause.
questions.topic: Mark the Phrase Breaks - Usage Debates and Style Guides

questions.prompt: A style guide specifies an em dash without surrounding spaces to set off an unexpected clarification. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: The formula was incomplete — we needed one more measurement.
The formula was incomplete - we needed one more measurement.
The formula was incomplete—we needed one more measurement.
The formula was incomplete--we needed one more measurement.
questions.explanation: The sentence uses a closed em dash to set off the clarification without spaces on either side.
questions.skill: Using an em dash for an unexpected clarification

questions.prompt: A style guide requires a colon to introduce an explanation. Which sentence follows that rule?
choices: The coach offered one strategy, defend the center early.
The coach offered one strategy; defend the center early.
The coach offered one strategy: defend the center early.
The coach offered one strategy: and defend the center early.
questions.explanation: The colon correctly introduces the explanation of the strategy the coach offered.
questions.skill: Using a colon before an explanation

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses an en dash to indicate a numeric range?
choices: The study covered the years 2010-2020.
The study covered the years 2010–2020.
The study covered the years 2010 to 2020.
The study covered the years 2010—2020.
questions.explanation: The correct sentence uses an en dash without spaces to indicate a numeric range.
questions.topic: Mark the Phrase Breaks - Usage Debates and Style Guides

questions.prompt: A style guide uses a semicolon to separate two parallel series when each series contains an internal comma. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: The workshop covers planning, editing; peer review, publication.
The workshop covers planning and editing; peer review and publication.
The workshop covers planning, editing, peer review, publication.
The workshop covers planning, editing: peer review, publication.
questions.explanation: The semicolon divides the two parallel series, and each series contains an internal comma.
questions.skill: Separating grouped series with a semicolon

questions.prompt: Which sentence follows American convention for placing a period inside closing quotation marks?
choices: The notice said, "Do not enter."
The notice said, "Do not enter".
The notice said, "Do not enter"?
The notice said, "Do not enter"
questions.explanation: The correct sentence follows American style by placing the period inside the closing quotation marks.
questions.topic: Mark the Phrase Breaks - Usage Debates and Style Guides

questions.prompt: A style guide requires a comma after an introductory interjection. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: The robot completed the obstacle course, amazing.
Amazing; the robot completed the obstacle course.
Amazing, the robot completed the obstacle course.
Amazing the robot completed the obstacle course.
questions.explanation: The introductory interjection Amazing is set off from the main clause by a comma.

questions.prompt: A style guide says a compound predicate should not be separated by a comma. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: The club reviewed, the proposal and approved it.
The club reviewed the proposal, and approved it.
The club, reviewed the proposal and approved it.
The club reviewed the proposal and approved it.
questions.explanation: Reviewed the proposal and approved it is a compound predicate, so no comma belongs between the two verbs.

questions.prompt: A style guide places the comma before a quotation and the question mark inside it. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: The librarian asked: 'May I borrow another book?'
The librarian asked, 'May I borrow another book?'
The librarian asked 'May I borrow another book?'
The librarian asked, 'May I borrow another book'.
questions.explanation: The sentence places a comma before the quotation and a question mark inside it as the stated style guide requires.
questions.skill: Punctuating a direct question within a quotation

questions.prompt: A style guide prohibits a comma between a linking verb and its predicate adjective. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: The final result was, surprising indeed.
The final result was, surprising.
The final result, was surprising.
The final result was surprising.
questions.explanation: A linking verb joins directly to its predicate adjective without a comma.
questions.topic: Usage Debates and Style Guides — Marking Phrase Breaks

questions.prompt: A style guide requires a comma after an introductory absolute phrase. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: With the lights dimmed the audience settled into silence.
With the lights dimmed, the audience settled into silence.
With the lights, dimmed the audience settled into silence.
With the lights dimmed; the audience settled into silence.
questions.explanation: The comma marks the phrase break after the introductory absolute phrase With the lights dimmed.
questions.skill: Marking the break after an introductory absolute phrase

questions.prompt: Two independent clauses are joined to show a close relationship. Which sentence is punctuated correctly with a semicolon?
choices: Because rain flooded the court; the game was moved indoors.
Rain flooded the court; the game was moved indoors.
Rain flooded the court, the game was moved indoors; spectators left early.
Rain flooded the court; and the game was moved indoors.
questions.explanation: The semicolon correctly joins two independent clauses without a coordinating conjunction.
questions.skill: Joining independent clauses with a semicolon

questions.prompt: A style guide requires commas around a parenthetical phrase that interrupts the main sentence. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: The pianist, unable to stop coughing, continued the performance.
The pianist unable to stop coughing continued the performance.
The pianist, unable to stop coughing continued the performance.
The pianist unable to stop coughing, continued the performance.
questions.explanation: The paired commas set the phrase unable to stop coughing apart from the surrounding main clause.
questions.topic: Mark the Phrase Breaks - Usage Debates and Style Guides

questions.prompt: A style guide requires a comma before "etc." when it follows a list of three or more items. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: The kit includes ropes, hooks, carabiners etc.
The kit includes ropes, hooks, carabiners. etc.
The kit includes ropes, hooks, carabiners; etc.
The kit includes ropes, hooks, carabiners, etc.
questions.explanation: The guide places a comma before "etc." after a list of three or more items.
questions.topic: Mark the Phrase Breaks - Usage Debates and Style Guides

questions.prompt: A style guide requires a hyphen in decision-making when it modifies a noun. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: The decision making team approved the proposal.
The decisionmaking team approved the proposal.
The decision making-team approved the proposal.
The decision-making team approved the proposal.
questions.explanation: The hyphen joins decision and making in the compound adjective decision-making.
questions.skill: Using a style guide to hyphenate compound modifiers

questions.prompt: A style guide says no comma is needed before "but also" in a "not only … but also" construction. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: Not only did she finish the race, but also she set a record.
Not only did she finish the race, but also, she set a record.
Not only did she finish the race but also she set a record.
Not only did she finish the race but also, she set a record.
questions.explanation: The guide omits the comma before "but also" in the correlative pair.
questions.topic: Mark the Phrase Breaks - Usage Debates and Style Guides

questions.prompt: A style guide requires a comma after the salutation of a personal letter. Which punctuation mark should follow Dear Maya?
choices: Dear Maya.
Dear Maya;
Dear Maya:
Dear Maya,
questions.explanation: A comma follows the salutation and separates it from the body of the letter.
questions.skill: Applying a style-guide rule for letter salutations

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly avoids placing a phrase break between a complete subject and its verb?
choices: The results of the survey were surprising.
The results of the survey; were surprising.
The results of the survey: were surprising.
The results of the survey, were surprising.
questions.explanation: The subject The results of the survey should not be separated from the verb were by punctuation.

questions.prompt: A style guide prohibits a comma before because when it joins two independent clauses. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: The meeting ended early because, the speaker lost track of time.
The meeting ended early, because the speaker lost track of time.
The meeting ended early because the speaker lost track of time.
The meeting ended early because the speaker, lost track of time.
questions.explanation: Because introduces a dependent clause that belongs directly after the independent clause without a separating comma.
questions.skill: Applying style-guide rules for dependent clauses

questions.prompt: A style guide requires commas around the title of a book when the title stands alone within a sentence. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: The novel The Silent Orchard won an award.
The novel The Silent Orchard, won an award.
The novel, The Silent Orchard won an award.
The novel, The Silent Orchard, won an award.
questions.explanation: The paired commas show that The Silent Orchard is a stand-alone title interrupting the main sentence.
questions.skill: Marking phrase breaks around book titles

questions.prompt: A style guide requires a comma after an introductory infinitive phrase. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: To finish the race, Lina sprinted toward the finish line.
To finish the race: Lina sprinted toward the finish line.
To finish the race Lina sprinted toward the finish line.
To finish the race; Lina sprinted toward the finish line.
questions.explanation: The comma after To finish the race closes the introductory infinitive phrase.
questions.topic: Mark the Phrase Breaks - Usage Debates and Style Guides

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly sets off the transitional phrase 'for example' with commas?
choices: Many birds migrate south for the winter; for example; the swallow and the warbler.
Many birds migrate south for the winter for example the swallow and the warbler.
Many birds migrate south for the winter, for example, the swallow and the warbler.
Many birds migrate south for the winter — for example — the swallow and the warbler.
questions.explanation: The correct sentence places commas before and after the transitional phrase 'for example'.
questions.topic: Mark the Phrase Breaks - Usage Debates and Style Guides

questions.prompt: A style guide says not to place a comma before and when it joins two short independent clauses. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: The bell rang, and we left.
The bell rang, we left.
The bell rang and we left.
The bell rang and, we left.
questions.explanation: The guide omits the comma before and because the two short independent clauses are joined directly.
questions.topic: Mark the Phrase Breaks - Usage Debates and Style Guides

questions.prompt: A style guide requires a prepositional phrase to remain unbroken, with no comma inside it. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: The hikers followed, the marked trail to the summit.
The hikers followed the marked, trail to the summit.
The hikers followed the marked trail to the summit.
The hikers followed the marked trail, to the summit.
questions.explanation: The prepositional phrases following followed remain complete and unbroken in the correctly punctuated sentence.
questions.topic: Usage Debates and Style Guides — Marking Phrase Breaks

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly marks the phrase breaks around an appositive that renames the subject?
choices: The captain a senior guard called, the final timeout.
The captain a senior guard, called the final timeout.
The captain, a senior guard called the final timeout.
The captain, a senior guard, called the final timeout.
questions.explanation: The first sentence uses a pair of commas to set off the appositive that renames the captain.

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly places a comma before the final 'too' meaning 'also'?
choices: She wants to join the team — too.
She wants to join the team too.
She wants to join the team; too.
She wants to join the team, too.
questions.explanation: The correct sentence includes a comma before the final 'too' to indicate addition.
questions.topic: Mark the Phrase Breaks - Usage Debates and Style Guides

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly marks the phrase breaks around a nonrestrictive relative clause?
choices: Priya's camera, which she bought in June has a cracked lens.
Priya's camera which she bought in June, has a cracked lens.
Priya's camera, which she bought in June, has a cracked lens.
Priya's camera which, she bought in June, has a cracked lens.
questions.explanation: The first sentence sets off a nonrestrictive relative clause with a comma before and after the clause.
questions.skill: Marking phrase breaks around nonrestrictive clauses

questions.prompt: A style guide requires a colon before a quotation that presents the speaker’s complete message. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: The director said: 'The meeting begins now.'
The director said, 'The meeting begins now.'
The director said 'The meeting begins now.'
The director said: 'The meeting begins now,'
questions.explanation: The colon introduces the quoted statement, and the period completes the sentence inside the quotation.

questions.prompt: A style guide requires a comma before a parenthetical phrase that comes at the end of a sentence. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: The museum reopened on Friday, after months of repairs.
The museum reopened on Friday after months, of repairs.
The museum, reopened on Friday after months of repairs.
The museum reopened on Friday; after months of repairs.
questions.explanation: The comma sets off the final parenthetical phrase after months of repairs from the main sentence.
questions.skill: Setting off a final parenthetical phrase

questions.prompt: A style guide requires a comma after an introductory participial phrase. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: Running late the team hurried to the field.
Running late, the team hurried to the field.
Running late; the team hurried to the field.
Running late: the team hurried to the field.
questions.explanation: The comma after Running late closes the introductory participial phrase before the main clause begins.
questions.topic: Mark the Phrase Breaks - Usage Debates and Style Guides

questions.prompt: A style guide uses square brackets to set off a brief nonessential phrase. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: The hikers (who arrived early) started the first ascent.
The hikers [who arrived early] started the first ascent.
The hikers, who arrived early, started the first ascent.
The hikers [who arrived early started the first ascent.
questions.explanation: The square brackets correctly enclose and set off the nonessential phrase who arrived early.
questions.topic: Usage Debates and Style Guides — Marking Phrase Breaks

questions.prompt: A style guide requires a serial comma in every list of three or more items. Which sentence follows the rule?
choices: The assignment required research, citations and a bibliography.
The assignment required research and citations, plus a bibliography.
The assignment required research, citations, and, a bibliography.
The assignment required research, citations, and a bibliography.
questions.explanation: This list uses a serial comma before and to separate all three items correctly.
